claims.text: IPU states that, although Tonga has no political parties, some 2021 candidates ran under the banners of two political groups: the Democratic Party of the Friendly Islands (PTOA) and the Tonga People's Party (TPP). It reports three members elected on PTOA tickets.
claims.uncertainty: An interparliamentary summary, not a registration record. It expands the acronym but does not establish a legal identity, statute or continuity with earlier observations.

claims.text: IPU states that Prime Minister Pohiva Tu'i'onetoa was elected under the TPP banner at the 18 November 2021 election.
claims.uncertainty: An electoral-banner observation. Candidates formally stood as independents; this is not a party-office appointment.

claims.text: IPU states that on 15 December 2021 the newly elected Assembly held its first session and elected Siaosi Sovaleni (independent) as the new Prime Minister, defeating 'Aisake Eke (independent), whom the outgoing Prime Minister Tu'i'onetoa backed. The same page describes the process led by the interim Speaker as electing a Prime Minister Designate.
claims.locator: 'About the election', second paragraph; 'Other notes on the elections'
claims.uncertainty: IPU's 'elected as Prime Minister' describes the Assembly's selection. The royal appointment instrument and its effective date are not in this source and are not inferred.
